title: Naturality of the coherently normalized integral Koszul braiding
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, and a scheme $W$ on which $\ell$ is invertible in every residue field. Use the completed integral constructible category and its completed derived tensor $T^{\mathrm{int}}_{E,W}$ together with the coherently reduction-normalized integral Koszul braiding $\beta^{\mathrm{int}}_{M,N}:T^{\mathrm{int}}_{E,W}(M,N)\xrightarrow{\sim}T^{\mathrm{int}}_{E,W}(N,M)$ of [def-pod-integral-tensor-constraints]. For arbitrary integral arrows $a:M\to M'$ and $b:N\to N'$, the braiding is natural:
$$\beta^{\mathrm{int}}_{M',N'}\circ T^{\mathrm{int}}_{E,W}(a,b)=T^{\mathrm{int}}_{E,W}(b,a)\circ\beta^{\mathrm{int}}_{M,N}.$$
No finite-field, perfectness, boundedness beyond the constructible integral category, or torsion-freeness hypothesis is added.

source.place: Tag 0FPQ (lemma-symmetric-monoidal-cat-complexes), signed total symmetry and its naturality; specialization to the coherently reduction-normalized completed integral tensor

proof.text: Write $\mathcal R_W$ for coherent reduction to derived strict systems and $\otimes^{\mathrm{sys}}$ for the derived tensor of strict systems, i.e. the derived tensor of module sheaves on the ringed sequence site [def-coef-ringed-sequence-site]. The integral tensor $T^{\mathrm{int}}_{E,W}$ is the derived inverse limit of the levelwise derived tensors of the reductions, functorially in both arguments [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], and the reduction/tensor comparison $c_{M,N}:\mathcal R_WT^{\mathrm{int}}_{E,W}(M,N)\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal R_WM\otimes^{\mathrm{sys}}\mathcal R_WN$ is obtained by applying the counit of the adjunction $\mathcal R_W\dashv\mathcal L_W$ to the levelwise tensor comparison [def-pur-completed-pullback-tensor-comparison]. Since $\mathcal R_W$ is a functor on the derived category and the unit, counit and all comparisons are natural for morphisms of the inputs [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus], $c$ is natural: $c_{M',N'}\circ\mathcal R_W(T^{\mathrm{int}}_{E,W}(a,b))=(\mathcal R_Wa\otimes^{\mathrm{sys}}\mathcal R_Wb)\circ c_{M,N}$, and likewise for $T^{\mathrm{int}}_{E,W}(b,a)$. By [def-pod-integral-tensor-constraints], $\mathcal R_W(\beta^{\mathrm{int}}_{M,N})=c_{N,M}^{-1}\circ\sigma_{\mathcal R_WM,\mathcal R_WN}\circ c_{M,N}$, where $\sigma$ is the strict-system braiding.

source.place: Tag 0FPQ (lemma-symmetric-monoidal-cat-complexes), signed total symmetry and its naturality; specialization to the coherently reduction-normalized completed integral tensor

proof.text: The strict-system braiding is the canonical derived symmetry of the ringed sequence site [def-pur-ringed-site-signed-tensor-models]: a natural isomorphism $\sigma:\otimes^{\mathrm{sys}}\xrightarrow{\sim}\otimes^{\mathrm{sys}}\circ\mathrm{swap}$ represented on flat-term K-flat complexes by the signed total swap $x\otimes y\mapsto(-1)^{ij}y\otimes x$ on bidegree $(i,j)$. Hence for the reduced arrows $\mathcal R_Wa,\mathcal R_Wb$, arbitrary morphisms of the derived category and not necessarily chain maps, $\sigma_{\mathcal R_WM',\mathcal R_WN'}\circ(\mathcal R_Wa\otimes^{\mathrm{sys}}\mathcal R_Wb)=(\mathcal R_Wb\otimes^{\mathrm{sys}}\mathcal R_Wa)\circ\sigma_{\mathcal R_WM,\mathcal R_WN}$. For chain maps $u,v$ between flat-term K-flat complexes this is the direct check: both composites send $x\otimes y$ to $(-1)^{ij}v(y)\otimes u(x)$. The signed swap commutes with $d(x\otimes y)=dx\otimes y+(-1)^ix\otimes dy$, so it is a chain map.

source.place: Tag 0FPQ (lemma-symmetric-monoidal-cat-complexes), signed total symmetry and its naturality

proof.text: Substituting Step 1 and Step 2, $\mathcal R_W(\beta^{\mathrm{int}}_{M',N'}\circ T^{\mathrm{int}}_{E,W}(a,b))=c_{N',M'}^{-1}\circ\sigma\circ(\mathcal R_Wa\otimes^{\mathrm{sys}}\mathcal R_Wb)\circ c_{M,N}=c_{N',M'}^{-1}\circ(\mathcal R_Wb\otimes^{\mathrm{sys}}\mathcal R_Wa)\circ\sigma\circ c_{M,N}=\mathcal R_W(T^{\mathrm{int}}_{E,W}(b,a)\circ\beta^{\mathrm{int}}_{M,N})$; the middle comparisons $c_{N,M}$ cancel. Both composites are morphisms $T^{\mathrm{int}}_{E,W}(M,N)\to T^{\mathrm{int}}_{E,W}(N',M')$ between derived-complete bounded constructible integral objects, because the integral tensor preserves this category [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. Coherent reduction is fully faithful, hence faithful, on that category by [lem-pod-integral-system-reduction-fully-faithful], so the two integral composites are equal. The argument applies to arbitrary $a$ and $b$, including identity and zero arrows and the zero object. No finite-field, perfectness, boundedness or torsion-freeness assumption is used beyond the constructible integral category.
